newsitem.title: FRANCE: BNP, Paribas to lead France Telecom sale.
newsitem.headline: BNP, Paribas to lead France Telecom sale.

text.p: The French finance and economy ministry said in a statement that banks Banque Nationale de Paris (BNP) and Banque Paribas had been designated global coordinators for the pending Bourse introduction of state-owned France Telecom.
The statement said the two banks would assure the coordination of the operation which would include both a public sale as well as a private placement with institutional investors.
The government is expected to sell a first tranche of 20 percent in the company in April in a partial privatisation ahead of full telecommunications liberalisation in 1998.
The government has said that it will ultimately keep a 51 percent stake in the operator, currently France's most profitable company valued at between 100 and 200 billion francs.
The France Telecom sale will follow the November 18 flotation of some 500 million shares in Germany's Deutsche Telekom.
Italy's Stet is expected to come to the market in late 1997.
